title: Exact moment support cut the required higher-order terms by 42 to 54 percent in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested which exact joint-failure moments identify loss of at least half of cleft-size weight in selected mouse contact models. We used 1,512 Allen V1 Deep Dive connections and 1,438 MICrONS connections, with three through eight observed contacts. With single and pair moments already known, nonzero terms in the event polynomial required 4,505 and 6,932 higher-order moments. These totals are 42.1 and 53.8 percent below all terms through the event degree. A signed state-mass perturbation proves that each nonzero term can be necessary at a law with positive mass in every state. An independent audit checked 112 event patterns and 4,865 exact omission witnesses. This is an extension of earlier bounds on the same data. It is not a new polynomial method or a release measurement. Exact structural weights, unrestricted dependence, selected incomplete arbors, and one animal per map limit the result. Moment counts do not give trial or recording cost. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes, and verified external retrieval instructions support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Mean number of higher-order moment terms under three exact identification rules. Single and pair moments are assumed known. These are descriptive model requirements, not animal confidence intervals or recording costs.
